name: Active Backup for Business
approval_note: Recommended for protecting staff laptops and servers; install version 3.2.1-25059 or later.
summary: Central, licence-free backup of company PCs, Macs, servers, virtual machines and file servers to the NAS.
description: Active Backup for Business backs up Windows and Mac computers, physical servers, VMware and Hyper-V virtual machines, and file servers to the NAS from one console. It keeps deduplicated, versioned backups on a schedule and can restore anything from a single file to a whole machine. There are no per-device licence fees on supported Synology models.
use_cases:
Engineering: back up the laptops field engineers take to commissioning sites, so a lost or damaged laptop does not lose project files and HMI programs.
Finance: back up the PC that runs the accounting software every night, so it can be restored in full after a disk failure or ransomware.
SWE: back up development servers and Hyper-V or VMware test VMs, and restore a whole VM after a failed update.
IT: let staff restore their own deleted files through the Active Backup for Business Portal instead of raising a request.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Active Backup for Business and click Install; SMB Service, which it depends on, is set up with it.
Open Active Backup for Business from Main Menu and activate it with the company IT Synology Account when asked.
Make sure backups go to a shared folder on a Btrfs volume, then set the default schedule and retention under Settings > Template.
Install the Active Backup for Business Agent from the Synology Download Center on each Windows PC or Mac, enter the NAS address and a DSM account, and check the device appears in the PC tab.
For virtual machines, open the Virtual Machine tab, add the VMware vSphere or Microsoft Hyper-V host, and create a backup task for the VMs you need.
For file servers, open the File Server tab, add the server's SMB or rsync details and create a task.
After the first backup, test a restore through the Active Backup for Business Portal and create recovery media for full-machine restores.
tips:
Install version 3.2.1-25059 or later: it fixes CVE-2026-15716 and Hyper-V backups and restores that fail after a Windows Defender update.
Backups on the same NAS are not offsite. Copy them to another site or to Synology C2 with Hyper Backup.
Full-machine backups use a lot of disk space and bandwidth; schedule them after office hours and watch volume usage in Storage Manager.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Web portal, Desktop app, Background service
keywords: backup pc, laptop backup, server backup, vm backup, restore files, ransomware recovery, hyper-v, vmware, abb

name: Active Backup for Business Agent (DSM)
approval_note: Needs a second Synology NAS running Active Backup for Business as the backup target.
summary: Backs up our whole NAS, including settings and packages, to a second NAS running Active Backup for Business.
description: Active Backup for Business Agent (DSM) lets a Synology NAS back itself up in full, including system configuration, packages and user data. The backups go to a remote Synology NAS running Active Backup for Business, which stores and manages the versions. It is meant for rebuilding a whole NAS after a hardware failure or disaster.
use_cases:
IT: keep a full image of the Puchong HQ NAS on a second Synology NAS at another office, so the whole system can be rebuilt after a fire, flood or hardware failure.
Management: shorten downtime after a major NAS failure, because settings and packages come back together with the data.
Finance: get the accounting shared folders and their permissions back in one restore, without IT re-creating them by hand.
how_to:
Check on Synology's compatibility page that our NAS model supports Active Backup for Business Agent (DSM); it needs DSM 7.2 or later.
On the backup NAS, install Active Backup for Business and review the default settings for DSM backups under Settings > Template.
On the NAS you want to protect, go to Main Menu > Package Center, install Active Backup for Business Agent (DSM) and open it.
Click Start, enter the backup NAS address (IP or domain name) and an account on it, then click Connect.
Restart DSM when prompted to apply the settings, ideally after office hours.
On the backup NAS, confirm in Active Backup for Business that the first backup finished.
tips:
A full-system backup can only be restored to the same NAS model or its successor, with at least as many drives in the same slots.
Put the backup NAS in a different office or building, so one site problem cannot destroy both units.
keywords: nas backup, full system backup, disaster recovery, backup whole nas, nas image, abb agent, restore nas

name: Active Backup for Google Workspace
approval_note: Free on supported Synology NAS models; set it up only if KLAE's email and files run on Google Workspace.
summary: Backs up company Google Workspace mail, Drive, shared drives, calendars and contacts to the NAS.
description: Active Backup for Google Workspace copies Gmail, Google Drive (My Drive and shared drives), Contacts and Calendar for company accounts onto the NAS. It can run in continuous backup mode or on a schedule, and keeps versions so deleted or overwritten items can be recovered. Staff can browse and restore their own items through a web portal.
use_cases:
Sales: recover a customer email thread or a quotation in Google Drive that was deleted by mistake or lost when a salesperson left.
HR: keep a copy of a departing employee's mailbox and Drive files after the Google account is removed.
Management: hold an independent copy of company email and documents outside Google, in case an account is compromised.
IT: let staff restore their own files and emails through the portal instead of raising a request.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Active Backup for Google Workspace and click Install; Universal Search is installed with it.
Follow the package's setup guide to create a Google service account with the required API access and domain-wide delegation in the Google Cloud and Google Admin consoles.
Open Active Backup for Google Workspace, create a task, and enter the Google Workspace admin email and the service account key file.
Select the services (Drive, shared drives, Gmail, Contacts, Calendar) and the accounts to protect, and turn on auto-discovery so new staff accounts are added.
Choose continuous or scheduled backup and set a retention policy.
Tell staff they can open the Active Backup for Google Workspace Portal to browse and restore their own items.
tips:
The service account can read every company mailbox and Drive, so only IT should hold its key file.
The first backup of large mailboxes and Drives takes a long time and needs plenty of NAS space.
If KLAE uses Microsoft 365 rather than Google Workspace, use Active Backup for Microsoft 365 instead.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Web portal, Background service
keywords: gmail backup, google drive backup, google workspace, restore email, deleted email, shared drive, g suite

name: Active Backup for Microsoft 365
approval_note: Free on supported Synology NAS models; set it up only if KLAE uses Microsoft 365, and keep it on version 3.0.0 or later.
summary: Backs up company Microsoft 365 email, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams data to the NAS for easy recovery.
description: Active Backup for Microsoft 365 copies Exchange Online mail, calendars and contacts, OneDrive for Business, SharePoint Online sites and Microsoft Teams data onto the NAS. It keeps versions so deleted or overwritten items can be restored, and staff can recover their own items through a web portal. Version 3.0.0 moves mail, calendar and contacts backup to Microsoft Graph ahead of Microsoft's October 2026 retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS).
use_cases:
Sales: recover a customer email or quotation attachment deleted from Outlook or OneDrive, even after the Microsoft recycle bin has been emptied.
HR: keep a former employee's mailbox and OneDrive files after the Microsoft 365 licence is removed.
Engineering: restore a SharePoint or Teams folder of commissioning reports after files are overwritten or deleted.
Management: hold a copy of company email and documents outside Microsoft, in case an account is compromised or ransomware syncs into OneDrive.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Active Backup for Microsoft 365 and click Install; Universal Search is installed with it.
Open Active Backup for Microsoft 365, create a task and sign in with a Microsoft 365 global administrator so the wizard can register the app in Microsoft Entra ID.
Select the services (mail, calendar, contacts, OneDrive, SharePoint, Teams) and the accounts to protect, and turn on auto-discovery for new staff.
Set the backup schedule and retention policy.
Give staff permission to use the Active Backup for Microsoft 365 Portal so they can browse and restore their own items.
Check the task status and logs after the first backup completes.
tips:
Microsoft retires EWS in October 2026. Update to version 3.0.0 or later and update the Entra ID app credentials in each task, or mail backups and restores may fail.
Once EWS is disabled, restores to Exchange use Mailbox Import; some other services still use EWS during the transition.
The admin and app credentials give access to every mailbox, so only IT should hold them.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Web portal, Background service
keywords: outlook backup, email backup, onedrive backup, sharepoint backup, teams backup, office 365, restore email, exchange

name: Active Insight
approval_note: It shares system health and performance data with Synology's cloud.
summary: Synology cloud service that watches NAS health and performance and warns IT before problems grow.
description: Active Insight sends health, performance and event data from the NAS to Synology's cloud, where IT can see dashboards and receive automated warnings. It can monitor several Synology systems in one place and helps Synology technical support diagnose problems faster.
use_cases:
IT: get a warning when a drive shows errors, a volume is nearly full or performance drops, before staff notice.
IT: watch the HQ NAS and any NAS at regional offices from one web dashboard, without logging in to each one.
Management: get faster answers from Synology support when there is a NAS problem.
Finance: avoid surprise downtime of accounting folders at month-end, because IT is warned early about failing hardware.
how_to:
Open Main Menu > Active Insight on the NAS and sign in with the company IT Synology Account.
Go to insight.synology.com and sign in with the same Synology Account to see the dashboard for our NAS.
In the notification settings, add the email addresses of everyone in the IT team so alerts do not depend on one person.
Review the performance graphs and event history when staff report slowness or errors.
Mention Active Insight when opening a Synology support ticket, so support can use the collected data.
tips:
Use a shared IT Synology Account rather than a personal one.
It sends system and performance data to Synology's cloud; confirm this fits KLAE's data policy.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Web portal, Background service
keywords: monitoring, nas health, alerts, performance, disk failure warning, support ticket, system status

name: ActiveProtect Vault
approval_note: No business need unless KLAE buys Synology ActiveProtect backup appliances.
summary: Remote, tamper-proof backup storage for Synology ActiveProtect appliances; not useful without them.
description: ActiveProtect Vault turns a Synology NAS into remote storage for Synology ActiveProtect, a separate line of dedicated backup appliances. It keeps backup copies in WORM (write once, read many) vaults that cannot be changed before their retention ends, limits access to administrators, and lets IT choose the TLS encryption level. It runs on Container Manager.
use_cases:
IT: only if KLAE later buys ActiveProtect appliances, keep a second, unchangeable copy of their backups on a NAS at another office.
Management: meet a customer or auditor requirement for backups that cannot be altered or deleted, if ActiveProtect is adopted.
IT: for now, protect PCs, servers and shared folders with Active Backup for Business and Hyper Backup, which need no extra appliances.
how_to:
Confirm KLAE runs Synology ActiveProtect appliances; without them this package has no use.
On the NAS that will hold the copies, install Container Manager and then ActiveProtect Vault from Main Menu > Package Center.
Open ActiveProtect Vault, create a vault and choose its retention and TLS level.
Add the vault as a remote destination in the ActiveProtect appliance's management console.
Keep the number of DSM administrator accounts small, since only administrators can access the vault.
tips:
WORM data cannot be deleted before its retention ends, even by IT, so plan the space carefully.
It needs Container Manager, which uses extra RAM and CPU.
keywords: activeprotect, worm, immutable backup, backup vault, ransomware protection, tamper proof

name: Advanced Media Extensions
approval_note: Since version 4.0 the NAS no longer decodes these formats, so it adds little for KLAE.
summary: Video codec add-on; since version 4.0, H.264/H.265 decoding happens on your own device instead.
description: Advanced Media Extensions (AME) adds media codec support to DSM. From version 4.0.0-4025, processing of HEVC (H.265), AVC (H.264) and VC-1 media moved from the NAS to the viewing device, so files only play if that computer or phone supports the codec. AME 4.0 needs DSM 7.2.2 or later, and Surveillance Station uses Surveillance Video Extension for server-side H.264 instead.
use_cases:
Marketing: product and exhibition videos in H.264 or H.265 play on staff PCs and phones that support those codecs, with or without AME.
Engineering: save training-centre recordings as standard MP4 (H.264) so any device can play them.
IT: install AME only if a Synology package lists it as required.
how_to:
Check whether any installed package actually requires it; normal file sharing does not need it.
If one does, install it from Package Center.
For iPhone HEIC photos or HEVC videos without previews in Synology Photos, install Synology Image Assistant on staff computers instead.
For camera recordings, use Surveillance Video Extension with Surveillance Station rather than AME.
tips:
If the viewing device does not support the codec, playback of those files is limited.
Video Station was removed in DSM 7.2.2, so there is no video-library use for AME on DSM 7.2.2 or later.
keywords: codec, hevc, h.265, h.264, heic, video playback, media codec, ame

name: Antivirus by McAfee
approval_note: Paid licence after the trial; compare it with the free Antivirus Essential before buying.
summary: Paid antivirus that scans the NAS for viruses and malware using the McAfee engine.
description: Antivirus by McAfee scans the data and system partitions of the NAS for viruses and other malware, using McAfee's commercial scanning engine. IT can run manual scans or set scheduled scans, and virus definitions update automatically. It is a paid package with a free trial; version 1.6.1-4006 fixes false positives.
use_cases:
Sales: scan the shared quotation and customer folders so a file infected on one laptop is not passed on to customers or principals.
Engineering: check the folders where field engineers upload files copied from customer site PCs and USB drives after commissioning work.
Finance: lower the risk that an infected invoice or bank statement attachment saved to the NAS spreads to other staff PCs.
IT: run a scheduled full scan every weekend with a commercial engine, with virus definitions kept up to date automatically.
how_to:
If Antivirus Essential is installed, uninstall it first, because only one antivirus package should run at a time.
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Antivirus by McAfee and click Try to start the free trial.
Open Antivirus by McAfee from Main Menu and run a full scan to get a baseline.
Set up a scheduled scan for nights or weekends, outside office hours.
Check that automatic virus-definition updates are turned on.
Review any infected files the scans find, and buy a licence before the trial ends if KLAE decides to keep the package.
tips:
Run only one antivirus package on the NAS at a time; do not install it alongside Antivirus Essential.
Full scans use a lot of CPU and disk activity; schedule them outside office hours.
Antivirus does not replace backups; recovery from ransomware still depends on snapshots and Hyper Backup.
keywords: antivirus, virus scan, malware, mcafee, virus, security scan, infected file, trojan

name: Antivirus Essential
approval_note: Free Synology package; it needs at least 1 GB of RAM to run scans.
summary: Free antivirus that scans NAS files for viruses and malware, on demand or on a schedule.
description: Antivirus Essential is Synology's free antivirus package, based on the open-source ClamAV engine (upgraded to ClamAV 1.4.4 in version 1.6.1-4006). It runs full, custom or system scans, moves infected files to quarantine and updates virus definitions automatically. The latest version also fixes CVE-2026-20031 and some false positives.
use_cases:
Sales: scan shared folders of quotations, tenders and customer drawings so infected files are not emailed to customers.
Engineering: run a custom scan on the folder where engineers upload files from customer site PCs and USB drives.
Marketing: check folders of exhibition material and brochure files received from printers and agencies.
IT: run a weekly scheduled full scan and keep a record of anything found or quarantined.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Antivirus Essential and click Install.
Open Antivirus Essential and go to Update to download the latest virus definitions.
On Overview, choose Full scan for the whole NAS, Custom scan for chosen shared folders, or System scan for system areas.
Go to Scheduled Scan and create a weekly full scan outside office hours.
Check Quarantine after each scan; delete infected files or restore any that are false positives.
Use Logs to review past scans and Settings to adjust scan options.
tips:
Scanning needs at least 1 GB of RAM and uses CPU; schedule full scans at night or on weekends.
Run only one antivirus package at a time; do not install Antivirus by McAfee alongside it.
Keep the package updated, as new versions fix security issues such as CVE-2026-20031.
keywords: antivirus, virus scan, free antivirus, malware, clamav, quarantine, virus, security scan

name: Audio Station
approval_note: Entertainment app with no business need; store audio files in Synology Drive instead.
summary: Music library and streaming app; no business use at KLAE.
description: Audio Station organises music and audio files stored on the NAS for playback in the browser and on phones through the DS audio app. It supports playlists, internet radio and sharing. It is designed for home media use rather than office work.
use_cases:
Marketing: voice-overs and audio for product videos can be stored and previewed in Synology Drive without this app.
HR: background music for company events is easier to play from a laptop than to stream from the NAS.
IT: not installing it keeps personal music off company storage and means one less package to patch.
how_to:
Check with IT first; it is not recommended at KLAE.
If IT installs it for a specific need, open Main Menu > Audio Station; it lists audio files from the music shared folder.
Browse by album, artist or folder, and double-click a track to play it in the browser.
Create playlists, or use the DS audio mobile app to play the library on a phone.
tips: Do not store personal music on company storage; it takes backup space and may raise copyright issues.
keywords: music, audio, mp3, songs, playlist, streaming, radio, ds audio

name: Bitdefender for MailPlus
approval_note: Needs paid Bitdefender licences; weigh the cost against how much spam and malware we receive.
summary: Adds paid Bitdefender anti-spam and anti-virus engines to a Synology MailPlus company email server.
description: Bitdefender for MailPlus adds Bitdefender's commercial anti-spam and anti-virus engines to Synology MailPlus Server, so email is checked by Bitdefender for spam and viruses. It needs paid Bitdefender licences, which can be bought in advance with a chosen activation date. Version 1.1.0-20108 requires MailPlus Server 4.0.0 and DSM 7.2 or later.
use_cases:
Finance: catch more phishing emails with fake payment requests or changed bank details before they reach accounts staff.
Sales: reduce spam in enquiry and quotation mailboxes, so real customer RFQs are not buried.
HR: block malware hidden in attachments sent as job applications and CVs.
IT: add a commercial filtering engine when company email runs on MailPlus Server.
how_to:
In Main Menu > Package Center, check that Synology MailPlus Server is version 4.0.0 or later; update it first if needed.
Search Package Center for Bitdefender for MailPlus and click Install.
Buy Bitdefender licences for MailPlus; for a renewal, choose an activation date that starts when the current licence ends.
Activate the licences on the NAS, then open Synology MailPlus Server and turn on the Bitdefender anti-spam and anti-virus engines in its security settings.
Send a test email with the harmless EICAR antivirus test file and confirm it is blocked.
Ask staff to report spam that still gets through, and adjust the filter settings.
tips:
Licences can be bought ahead of time with a chosen activation date, so renewals do not leave a gap in protection.
It requires MailPlus Server 4.0.0 and DSM 7.2 or later; check versions before buying licences.
No filter catches everything; staff should still confirm by phone before paying a new invoice or changing a supplier's bank details.
keywords: spam, email virus, anti-spam, phishing, bitdefender, junk mail, email security, mailplus

name: C2 Identity Edge Server
approval_note: No use today; consider it only if KLAE subscribes to Synology C2 Identity.
summary: Local helper for Synology C2 Identity cloud accounts, so the NAS can check sign-ins quickly on site.
description: Synology C2 Identity is a cloud directory service for managing staff accounts. C2 Identity Edge Server runs on the NAS and retrieves directory information from C2 Identity, so that when C2 Identity users access on-premises resources, the NAS can authenticate them quickly. It is only relevant if KLAE adopts C2 Identity.
use_cases:
IT: if KLAE moves to C2 Identity, let staff at each regional office sign in to the local NAS with fast on-site authentication.
HR: with C2 Identity, create or disable a staff account once in the cloud and have the change apply to the NAS at every office.
Sales: use the same company account to open shared folders on a regional office NAS as at Puchong HQ.
Management: compare C2 Identity with Synology Directory Server before choosing one company-wide account system.
how_to:
Decide first whether KLAE will use Synology C2 Identity; without it this package has no use.
Set up the KLAE domain and staff accounts in the C2 Identity admin console.
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for C2 Identity Edge Server and click Install.
Open C2 Identity Edge Server and follow its setup to link the NAS to the KLAE C2 Identity domain.
Test that a C2 Identity user can sign in to the NAS and open the right shared folders.
tips:
C2 Identity is a paid cloud service; get management approval before setting it up.
Choose one directory system for the company: C2 Identity, Synology Directory Server or LDAP Server. Running several makes accounts harder to manage.
keywords: c2 identity, user accounts, cloud directory, login, single account, domain, identity, edge server

name: Central Management System
approval_note: Only useful if KLAE runs more than one Synology NAS, such as at regional offices.
summary: Manages several Synology NAS from one console: monitoring, shared settings, updates and delegated admin.
description: Central Management System (CMS) lets IT monitor and manage multiple Synology NAS from one host NAS. IT can group servers, create policies to change settings across a group at once, keep DSM and packages up to date, and delegate admin permissions per group or server. It is only useful when a company runs several Synology NAS, for example one per office.
use_cases:
IT: apply the same security, password and notification settings to every office NAS from HQ.
IT: roll out DSM and package updates to all office NAS units without logging in to each one.
IT: let a local IT contact at a regional office manage only that office's NAS, through delegated permissions.
Management: be sure every office NAS follows the same security standard.
how_to:
Choose one NAS (normally at HQ) as the CMS host and install Central Management System from Main Menu > Package Center (it needs DSM 7.2-64570 or later).
Open Central Management System and add each managed NAS with its address and an administrator account.
Organise the servers into groups, for example by office.
Create policies to apply the same settings to each group.
Use the update features to keep DSM and packages current across groups.
Delegate admin permissions per group or server where a local contact needs them, and check the overview for offline or unhealthy servers.
tips:
The CMS host has admin access to every NAS; protect its admin accounts with 2-factor authentication.
Connect remote office NAS units over a VPN, not by opening admin ports to the internet.
keywords: manage multiple nas, central management, branch office, policy, mass update, cms, regional office nas

name: Cloud Sync
approval_note: Each task sends company files to an outside cloud account, so IT reviews and sets up every link.
summary: Keeps NAS folders in sync with cloud services such as OneDrive, SharePoint, Google Drive and Dropbox.
description: Cloud Sync connects shared folders on the NAS with public cloud storage such as Microsoft OneDrive, Microsoft SharePoint, Google Drive, Google shared drives, Dropbox and Baidu Cloud. Each task can sync both ways, download only or upload only, with schedules, file filters and optional encryption. It keeps files the same in both places but is not a backup.
use_cases:
Sales: download-only sync of a principal's shared OneDrive or SharePoint price list folder into the NAS, so every office sees the latest prices.
Marketing: upload-only sync of final brochures and product photos to a Dropbox or Google Drive folder shared with the website agency.
Engineering: pull principals' updated datasheets and manuals from their cloud folders into the engineering library on the NAS.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Cloud Sync and click Install, then open it.
Choose the cloud provider and sign in with a company-owned cloud account, never a personal one.
Select the local shared folder and the remote folder to link.
Choose the sync direction (both ways, download only or upload only) and turn on data encryption if needed.
Set the schedule and file filters in the task settings.
Check the task status and history after the first sync.
tips:
Cloud Sync is not a backup: deleted or ransomware-encrypted files can sync to the other side. Use Hyper Backup for backups.
A Google shared drive holds at most 400,000 files and folders and up to 20 levels of subfolders; split large folders before syncing.
A large first sync can use a lot of internet bandwidth; run it after office hours.
keywords: onedrive, sharepoint, google drive, dropbox, cloud sync, sync to cloud, share with agency

name: DHCP Server
approval_note: Changes how a whole network gets IP addresses; a second DHCP server can cut staff off the network.
summary: Lets the NAS hand out IP addresses to devices on a network, a job the office router usually does.
description: DHCP Server lets the NAS automatically assign IP addresses, gateway and DNS settings to computers and devices on a LAN. It is set up per network interface and also supports vendor options and PXE network boot. Version 1.0.3-0052 fixes several security issues (CVE-2026-2291 and CVE-2026-4890 to CVE-2026-4893).
use_cases:
Engineering: give out addresses on a separate training-centre or test network for PLCs, HMIs and laptops, kept apart from the office LAN.
IT: use PXE to boot new office PCs from the network when installing or reimaging them.
IT: provide addresses for a small network whose router cannot act as a DHCP server.
how_to:
Confirm that no other DHCP server (usually the router or firewall) is active on the network you plan to serve.
Give the NAS network interface a fixed IP address in Control Panel > Network > Network Interface.
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for DHCP Server and click Install.
Open DHCP Server, go to Network Interface, select the interface and click Edit.
Tick Enable DHCP server, enter the DNS servers, lease time and the address range with subnet mask and gateway, then save.
Use the Vendor and PXE sections only if devices need vendor options or network boot.
Check the list of DHCP clients to confirm devices are receiving addresses.
tips:
Only one DHCP server should run on each network; two can give devices wrong addresses and break office connections.
The NAS must keep a fixed IP address while it acts as the DHCP server.
PXE boot also needs a TFTP server holding the boot files, which DSM provides under Control Panel > File Services.
keywords: dhcp, ip address, network, pxe, network boot, ip assignment, router, lan

name: DNS Server
approval_note: Once staff PCs use it, a DNS fault stops name lookups for the whole office.
summary: Runs the office's own DNS, so computers find the NAS and servers by name instead of IP address.
description: DNS Server, based on BIND 9.16.34, lets the NAS translate names into IP addresses, and back, for the local network. It can host several zones, forward other lookups to internet DNS servers and use views to give different answers to different clients. Synology Directory Server depends on it; this version requires DSM 7.2 or later.
use_cases:
Sales: open the NAS and internal web tools by an easy name instead of remembering an IP address.
Engineering: give fixed names to test servers, HMIs and lab equipment in the training centre, so demos do not depend on IP addresses.
SWE: point internal names at test and staging web apps hosted on the NAS.
IT: provide the DNS zone that Synology Directory Server needs to run a Windows domain.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for DNS Server and click Install.
Open DNS Server, go to Zones and click Create > Master Zone, then enter the internal domain name.
Select the zone, click Edit > Resource Record and add A records for the NAS and other internal servers.
Go to Resolution, tick Enable resolution services and enable forwarders, entering the ISP or public DNS servers for internet names.
Test from a PC by running nslookup against the NAS IP address.
When tests pass, set the router or DHCP server to give out the NAS as the DNS server.
tips:
If staff PCs use the NAS for DNS and it goes down, they also lose internet name lookups; keep a second DNS server configured.
Avoid .local as the internal domain name; it can conflict with Apple devices and printer discovery.
Synology Directory Server installs and uses this package; do not remove it while the domain is in use.
keywords: dns, domain name, name server, hostname, zone, nslookup, internal name, ip lookup

name: Document Viewer
approval_note: Runs on Container Manager and adds memory use; Universal Viewer and Synology Office may already cover most needs.
summary: View Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OpenDocument files in the browser and share protected links.
description: Document Viewer opens Microsoft Office and OpenOffice documents stored on the NAS in the browser, without downloading them or needing Office installed. Documents can be shared through an encryptable link with a validity period, a password or DSM login, and an option to block download and printing. It depends on Container Manager.
use_cases:
Sales: share a tender document or price schedule as a view-only link that cannot be downloaded or printed and expires after the closing date.
Management: read reports and board papers on any computer without installing Microsoft Office.
Engineering: open older .doc and .xls datasheets and manuals stored on the NAS straight from Synology Drive.
how_to:
Ask IT to review and install Document Viewer from Package Center; it depends on Container Manager.
Open Main Menu > Document Viewer, click Open (the folder icon), choose the document and click Select.
Or, in Synology Drive, preview a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file and choose View > Open in Document Viewer.
Use Zoom, Rotate, Show Thumbnails and Outlines on the toolbar to move around the document.
To share, click More > Share, set a Validity period, tick Enable secure sharing to require a DSM login or password, and tick Disable document download if needed.
tips:
Some formats, such as .rtf, .docm, .xlsm and Visio files, only display partly.
Blocking download also blocks printing, but readers can still take screenshots.
It runs through Container Manager and uses extra RAM and CPU; IT should check NAS memory before installing.
keywords: view word, open excel, document preview, docx viewer, read only share, view document, pptx viewer, no office installed

name: Download Station
approval_note: Peer-to-peer downloads bring copyright, malware and bandwidth risks, and it depends on end-of-life Python2.
summary: Downloads web, FTP and torrent files directly to the NAS; not recommended at KLAE.

IT: download a large firmware or software image overnight directly to the NAS without leaving a PC on.
Engineering: large configuration software installers from principals can be downloaded once by IT to a shared folder and installed from there.
Management: keeping BitTorrent off company equipment avoids copyright complaints against KLAE's internet line.

Install only after IT and management agree on a real need; it is not recommended at KLAE.

Open Main Menu > Download Station, create a new download task and paste the download URL.

Scan downloaded files with antivirus before sharing them with staff.

how_to:

Install DSM Agent from Package Center with an administrator account.
Open DSM Agent and ask a question in plain language, for example how to set up a backup task or what a storage warning means.
Turn on on-screen awareness only when you want it to use the open DSM window as context.
Check each answer against the Synology Knowledge Center before changing settings, and make changes outside office hours.
tips:
It is a new 1.0 release; keep it updated in Package Center, as early versions are still being fixed.
Never type passwords, licence keys or customer data into the chat.
Answers are based on Synology's documentation and can be generic; it does not replace Synology technical support.

name: File Station
approval_note: Part of DSM and available to every staff account.
summary: Browse, search, upload, download and share NAS files from your web browser.
description: File Station is the built-in file manager in DSM. It lets you open, search, upload, download and organise files and folders on the NAS from a web browser, and preview many file types without downloading them. You can also share files with people outside KLAE by sending a link instead of a large email attachment.
use_cases:
Sales: search the department shared folder for an old quotation or a principal's price list from any PC, without mapping a network drive.
Marketing: send a large product video or catalogue to an exhibition organiser as a password-protected link with an end date.
Engineering: upload commissioning photos and test reports from a customer site or regional office through the browser.
Finance: preview a supplier invoice PDF or a Synology Office spreadsheet in the browser before downloading it.
how_to:
Sign in to DSM with your NAS account and open Main Menu > File Station.
The left panel lists the shared folders you have permission to open. Click a folder to see its contents.
To find a file, type a name in the search box at the top right of the File Station window. Use the advanced search options to filter by file type, size or date.
To upload, drag files from your PC into the open folder, or click Upload. To download, select one or more files, right-click and choose Download (several files download as one zip file).
Double-click a file to preview it in the browser. Images, PDFs and Synology Office files open without downloading.
To share with someone outside KLAE, right-click the file or folder and choose Share. In the sharing window, set a password and an end date before you copy the link.
tips:
Always protect links for customers or suppliers with a password and an end date. You can review and delete your links in Tools > Shared Links Manager.
Deleted files can only be recovered if IT has turned on the Recycle Bin for that shared folder. Tell IT quickly if you delete something by mistake.
For files you edit every day or need offline on your laptop, use Synology Drive instead, which keeps version history.

name: Glacier Backup
approval_note: Amazon no longer accepts new Glacier customers, so KLAE cannot start using it; use Hyper Backup instead.
summary: Backs up NAS folders to Amazon Glacier, a legacy AWS archive service closed to new customers since Dec 2025.
description: Glacier Backup sends copies of shared folders to Amazon Glacier in the company's own AWS account for long-term archiving, with AWS storage and retrieval charges. Amazon stopped accepting new customers for this original vault-based Glacier service on 15 December 2025, and retrieving data can take hours. Updating the package to version 1.5.2 also installs PHP 8.0 automatically.
use_cases:
IT: none for new set-ups; send offsite copies to Synology C2 Storage or another NAS with Hyper Backup instead.
Finance: keep archives of closed financial years with Hyper Backup, which restores much faster.
Engineering: archive completed project files with Hyper Backup or Synology Tiering rather than a closed AWS service.
how_to:
Do not set up new Glacier Backup tasks; Amazon no longer accepts new Glacier accounts.
For offsite archives, install Hyper Backup from Main Menu > Package Center instead.
In Hyper Backup, choose Synology C2 Storage or a remote Synology NAS as the destination.
If an old Glacier Backup task is ever found, restore its data to the NAS, check it, then retire the task and the AWS vault.
tips:
Amazon charges for every retrieval and retrievals can take hours.
Amazon Glacier Deep Archive is not supported by this package.

name: Hybrid Share
approval_note: Each Hybrid Share folder adds to the paid C2 subscription, so only IT creates them.
summary: Shared folders kept in Synology C2 cloud with a fast local cache on the NAS, shareable across offices.
description: Hybrid Share keeps the full contents of selected shared folders in Synology C2 Storage while the NAS holds a local cache of recently used files for fast access. Staff use these folders like any other shared folder, and the same folder can be mounted on up to 10 Synology NAS at different sites for cross-site work, with end-to-end AES-256 encryption. It needs a paid C2 subscription, now called the OneStorage plan.
use_cases:
Sales: give HQ and any regional office with its own Synology NAS the same folder of price lists and quotation templates.
Engineering: keep large project and drawing archives in C2 without filling the NAS disks, while recent projects open quickly from the local cache.
Management: get key folders back quickly after a NAS failure or disaster, because the full data is already held in C2.
IT: avoid buying larger disks for folders that are mostly old files.
how_to:
Open Main Menu > Hybrid Share and link it to the company Synology Account that holds the C2 subscription.
Review the Hybrid Share folders, their local cache and the C2 storage used.
To add a folder, go to Control Panel > Shared Folder and mount a Hybrid Share folder or convert an existing shared folder.
Keep the C2 Encryption Key in a safe place outside the NAS.
Set user and group permissions in Control Panel > Shared Folder, the same as for normal folders.
To share a folder with another office, mount the same Hybrid Share folder on that office's Synology NAS.
tips:
Files not in the local cache are downloaded from C2 when opened, so they open more slowly and need a working internet link.
Without the Synology Account and C2 Encryption Key the data cannot be accessed; store the key safely.
Hybrid Share folders cannot be added to Synology Tiering plans.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Network drive, Background service
keywords: c2, cloud folder, hybrid cloud, multi site, branch office, cache, onestorage, share between offices

name: Hyper Backup
approval_note: Strongly recommended: it is the main way to keep an offsite copy of company files.
summary: Makes versioned, encrypted backups of NAS folders, apps and LUNs to C2 cloud, another NAS or a USB drive.
description: Hyper Backup copies shared folders, package data, system settings and LUNs from the NAS to other destinations: Synology C2 Storage, a second Synology NAS, a USB drive or public cloud storage. It keeps multiple deduplicated versions with rotation rules, can encrypt backups, and lets IT browse versions in Backup Explorer to restore files.
use_cases:
Finance: keep nightly offsite versions of accounting and payroll folders, so a fire, theft or ransomware attack at HQ does not destroy the only copy.
Sales: restore last week's version of the quotation and price list folders if files are overwritten or encrypted.
Engineering: keep long-term versions of project, commissioning and as-built documents that customers may ask for years later.
IT: send an encrypted copy to Synology C2 or a NAS at a regional office to follow the 3-2-1 backup rule.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Hyper Backup and click Install (it needs DSM 7.3 or later).
Open Hyper Backup, click + and choose Data backup task.
Pick a destination: Synology C2 Storage, a remote Synology NAS, a local USB drive or a supported cloud service.
Select the shared folders and applications to back up.
Turn on client-side encryption, backup integrity check and a rotation policy such as Smart Recycle, then set a nightly schedule.
Run the first backup, then test a restore by browsing versions in Backup Explorer.
tips:
Follow the 3-2-1 rule: three copies of data, on two types of storage, with one offsite.
Store the encryption password and key file outside the NAS; without them the backup cannot be restored.
Test a restore at least every quarter; a backup that has never been restored is not proven.
access: DSM web (Main Menu), Desktop app, Background service
keywords: backup, offsite backup, restore, c2 backup, usb backup, cloud backup, disaster recovery, 3-2-1, versions

name: Hyper Backup Vault
approval_note: Only useful with a second Synology NAS; install it on the NAS that receives the backups.
summary: Lets this NAS receive and store Hyper Backup copies sent from another Synology NAS.
description: Hyper Backup Vault is installed on the Synology NAS that receives backups. It lets other Synology NAS back up to it with Hyper Backup and shows an overview of all backup targets stored on it, with their logs and space used. It is useful when one office keeps the backups of another office's NAS.
use_cases:
IT: keep an offsite backup of the Puchong HQ NAS on a NAS at a regional office, and the reverse.
Management: keep backup copies on hardware KLAE owns, without monthly cloud storage fees.
Finance: have a second site hold copies of accounting folders, so a disaster at HQ does not stop month-end closing.
how_to:
On the receiving NAS (DSM 7.3 or later), go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Hyper Backup Vault and click Install.
Create a shared folder for incoming backups and a DSM account with permission to it for the sending NAS to use.
Allow the Hyper Backup Vault port (TCP 6281) between the two sites, preferably over a site-to-site VPN rather than the open internet.
On the sending NAS, create a Hyper Backup task with a remote Synology NAS as the destination and enter the receiving NAS address and account.
Open Hyper Backup Vault on the receiving NAS to check the backup targets, logs and storage used.
tips:
Place the receiving NAS in a different building or office from the source; a backup in the same room is not offsite.
Use a dedicated backup account and keep Hyper Backup client-side encryption on.
keywords: backup destination, remote backup, offsite backup, backup server, receive backups, vault

name: LDAP Server
approval_note: Changes how staff accounts are managed; decide between it and Synology Directory Server first.
summary: Holds one central set of staff accounts and groups that the NAS and other systems use for sign-in.
description: LDAP Server turns the NAS into a central directory of user accounts and groups for access control, authentication and account management. Other Synology NAS and LDAP-aware applications can use it to check sign-ins, so each person has one account. It can act as a provider server or as a consumer of another Synology LDAP Server, and includes backup and restore, user import and Google Workspace (G Suite) single sign-on.
use_cases:
HR: when a staff member joins or leaves, create or disable one account and their access to every connected NAS changes at once.
IT: let the NAS at each regional office use the same staff accounts as Puchong HQ by joining them to the HQ LDAP server.
IT: use LDAP users in RADIUS Server so staff sign in to office Wi-Fi with their own account.
SWE: let internal web apps check staff sign-ins against LDAP instead of keeping separate passwords.
how_to:
Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for LDAP Server and click Install.
Open LDAP Server, go to Settings and tick Enable LDAP Server.
Choose As the Provider server, enter the FQDN (the internal domain name) and an administrator password, then click Apply.
Note the Base DN and Bind DN shown in Settings; other systems need them to connect.
Create groups in Manage Groups and staff accounts in Manage Users, or import users from a file.
On other Synology NAS, join the directory in Control Panel > Domain/LDAP.
Use Backup and Restore to export the LDAP configuration regularly.
tips:
Windows PCs cannot join a plain LDAP directory; if staff PCs should sign in with company accounts, use Synology Directory Server instead.
Keep the LDAP administrator password in a safe place; it controls every staff account.
A regional office NAS can be set up as a consumer server that keeps a copy of the HQ directory.
keywords: ldap, user accounts, directory, login, staff accounts, single account, groups, authentication

name: Log Center
approval_note: Free Synology tool that helps IT investigate problems and security events.
summary: Collects logs from the NAS and network devices in one place, with search, alerts and archiving.
description: Log Center gathers and displays log messages from the NAS and from other network devices such as firewalls, switches and other NAS. use_cases:
IT: collect logs from the office firewall, switches and regional office NAS in one place, so problems can be traced from HQ.
Finance: help trace who changed, moved or deleted files in accounting folders, when file transfer logging is turned on.
Management: keep an archive of security and access logs for audits and incident reviews.
IT: get an email alert when repeated failed sign-ins or other critical events appear.

Go to Main Menu > Package Center, search for Log Center and click Install.
Open Log Center; Overview shows recent activity, and Logs lets you search and filter entries by date, level and keyword.
Go to Notifications and set rules to get an email when chosen events appear.
In Archive Settings, choose a shared folder and when old logs are archived.
To collect logs from other devices, create a rule in Log Receiving, then point the firewall, switch or other NAS to this NAS's IP address.
To copy this NAS's logs to another log server, set it up in Log Sending.
tips:
Set up email in Control Panel > Notification first, or Log Center cannot send alerts.
Received logs can grow quickly; set archive rules and keep them on a volume with free space.
Only accept logs from devices you trust, and limit the receiving port in the firewall.

name: Media Server
approval_note: Shares media with DLNA devices on the network without a login, so IT must review it first.

description: Media Server streams music, photos and videos from the NAS to DLNA/UPnP devices on the same local network, such as smart TVs and stereo systems. Those devices browse and play the files without signing in to DSM. It runs in the background; staff use it only through the TV or player.

Marketing: play product and company videos on a smart TV in the Puchong reception or showroom straight from the NAS.
Engineering: show training videos on the training centre TV without carrying USB drives.
IT: keep one central copy of display videos instead of separate USB sticks at each office.

Get approval, then install Media Server from Package Center.
Put display videos in a dedicated media folder that holds nothing confidential, and make sure it is indexed under Control Panel > Indexing Service.
Open Main Menu > Media Server and review General Settings, Browsing Settings and DMA Compatibility. Use DMA Compatibility to check which devices can see the media and block any that should not.
On the TV, open its media player or DLNA source and select the NAS.
Use a common format such as MP4 (H.264), because since AME 4.0 the NAS does not convert video for the TV.

DLNA has no password, so never index folders that contain confidential files.
Keep it on the office network only; it must not be exposed to the internet.

name: Migration Assistant
approval_note: One-off tool used only when IT replaces the NAS with a supported new model.
summary: Moves data, packages and settings from an old Synology NAS to a new one while staff keep working.
description: Migration Assistant is installed on a new (destination) Synology NAS to copy data, packages and system configuration from an older Synology NAS. Services stay available on the old NAS during the copy, and changes made meanwhile are synced before a short final switch-over. It is a one-off IT tool for replacing a NAS.
use_cases:
IT: move from the current NAS to a larger model without rebuilding users, permissions and shared folders by hand.
Sales: keep working on quotations during most of the migration, with only a short break at the final switch-over.
Management: keep a NAS replacement project to one short planned outage instead of a weekend shutdown.
how_to:
Check on Synology's website that both models are supported; the new NAS needs DSM 7.3 or later.
On the new NAS, create a storage pool equal to or larger than the old NAS's pool.
On the new NAS, go to Main Menu > Package Center and install Migration Assistant (version 1.1.1-1515 or later).
Open Migration Assistant and follow the wizard to connect to the old NAS and start the copy.
Let staff keep working on the old NAS while data copies, then schedule the final switch-over after office hours.
After the switch-over, check shared folders, permissions, packages and licences on the new NAS before retiring the old one.
tips:
All data and settings on the destination NAS are erased and replaced with those from the old NAS.
Licences, such as Surveillance Station camera licences, are not migrated and must be moved separately.
Use version 1.1.1-1515 or later, which fixes CVE-2026-88758.
keywords: migrate nas, new nas, replace nas, upgrade nas, move data, transfer settings

name: Note Station
approval_note: Free Synology package; fine for working notes, but final documents belong in Synology Drive.

It also has a to-do list, a web clipper browser extension, a desktop client and a mobile app.

Engineering: a shared troubleshooting notebook of known faults and fixes for HMIs, isolators and surge protectors.
Sales: record customer visit notes and follow-up to-dos in a notebook shared with the product specialist.
Management: keep meeting minutes and action lists in one notebook per regional office.
SWE: clip vendor documentation pages and keep API notes with the web clipper.

IT installs Note Station from Package Center.
Open it from Main Menu > Note Station in DSM.
Create a notebook (for example Customer Visits) and add notes to it. You can insert tables, images and attached files.
Add tags such as a customer or product name, and use the to-do list for follow-up actions, so you can find them later.
Share a note or a whole notebook with colleagues who need to read or edit it.
To work outside the browser, install Note Station Client on Windows or macOS, or the DS note app on your phone.

Notes are not ordinary files in Synology Drive; keep final reports and quotations in Drive.
If you encrypt a note with a password and forget it, the note cannot be recovered.

name: OAuth Service

summary: Lets approved third-party apps use NAS resources through OAuth 2.0 instead of staff passwords.
description: OAuth Service adds OAuth 2.0 to the NAS, so resource owners can authorise third-party apps to access NAS resources without sharing their passwords. IT: see in one place which apps staff have authorised, and remove access when an app is retired or a staff member leaves.
Management: approve integrations knowing each app only gets the access a user granted, and that access can be withdrawn without changing passwords.

Open Main Menu > OAuth Service.
On the Application tab, register each app that needs access to the NAS, and share its client credentials only with the developer or vendor.
On the Authorized Item tab, review which users have authorised which apps, and remove items that are no longer needed.
On the Log tab, check authorisation events regularly for apps or users you do not expect.
Include a check of Authorized Item in the staff exit checklist.
tips:
With Dynamic Client Registration, apps can register themselves, so check the Application list regularly for entries you do not recognise.
Treat client secrets like passwords. Never put them in shared folders or emails.

name: PDF Viewer
approval_note: Free and light Synology package; IT installs it. Drive already previews PDFs, so it is mainly for controlled sharing.
summary: Open, search and print PDFs on the NAS in the browser, and share them as protected links.
description: PDF Viewer displays PDF files stored on the NAS in the browser, with thumbnails, outlines, keyword search, attachments and printing. Sales: share a priced proposal PDF through a link that stops working after the tender closing date and cannot be downloaded.
Marketing: share a new catalogue PDF with a limited number of views before the public launch.
Engineering: search a long product manual or hazardous-area certificate for a keyword from any PC.

IT installs PDF Viewer from Package Center.
Open Main Menu > PDF Viewer, click Open (the folder icon), choose the PDF and click Select.
Click Search (the magnifying glass) to find words, or use Show Thumbnails and Outlines to jump between pages.
Click Print to print, or More > Download to save a copy.
To share, click More > Share, set the Validity period, tick Enable secure sharing for a password or DSM login, and tick Disable document download if the reader should not keep a copy. Then copy the link or QR code.
Edit or delete links later under More > Settings > Manage Shared Links.

Disable document download also stops the recipient from printing.
Delete links when a tender or project closes; deleted links stop working at once.

name: Presto File Server

summary: Fast transfer of large files over long distances between a PC and the NAS, or between two NAS. Licence needed.

Engineering: send large project drawings and commissioning videos between the Bintulu/Kuching office and HQ much faster than a normal upload.

IT: schedule regular transfers with Synology Presto Automator outside office hours, with bandwidth limits so daytime internet is not affected.

Check which network ports Presto needs for connections from outside the office, and open only those on the router.
Have a test user in a regional office install the Presto client on their computer, sign in with their NAS account and transfer a few large files.
Set up Synology Presto Automator for scheduled or repeated transfers.
Use the real-time connection monitoring to compare speeds with a normal upload before deciding to buy a licence.

The free trial can be used only once per NAS, so plan a real test period before starting it.
Presto helps with distance and latency, not with a slow internet line. Both ends still need decent bandwidth.

name: Proxy Server
approval_note: If it is installed but not used, IT should stop it.
summary: Caching web proxy that can block restricted websites; if it is installed but not used, stop it.
description: Proxy Server makes the NAS act as a caching proxy for HTTP-based services. PCs set to use it send their web traffic through the NAS, which can cache pages, keep logs and deny users access to restricted web services. The latest version fixes many security vulnerabilities (CVEs).
use_cases:
Engineering: limit the training centre PCs in Puchong to the websites needed for courses.
Procurement: limit shared warehouse PCs to the stock, supplier and courier websites staff need.
IT: if no PC uses the proxy, stop it to free NAS resources and close port 3128.
how_to:
Open Main Menu > Proxy Server and review the Settings tab: proxy port (3128), manager email, caching and logging.
If it is installed, check whether anything uses it: look at the proxy log, and check the proxy setting on a few office PCs (Windows Settings > Network & internet > Proxy).
If nothing uses it, open Proxy Server in Package Center and choose Stop. Uninstall it later once you are sure.
If it stays in use, add rules on the Access tab to deny restricted web services, and use the Authentication tab so requests are tied to named users.
Check the Cache tab so the cache does not take too much space on the volume.
tips:
Never forward port 3128 on the router. An open proxy can be abused by outsiders.
Keep it updated if you use it, since recent versions fix many security vulnerabilities.
keywords: proxy, web filter, block website, internet access, cache, website blocking, port 3128

name: QuickConnect
approval_note: IT limits which services it exposes and requires 2-step sign-in.
summary: Lets Synology apps reach the NAS over the internet with a QuickConnect ID, without router port forwarding.
description: QuickConnect lets client apps connect to the NAS from outside the office using a QuickConnect ID instead of an IP address, without setting up port forwarding on the router. Engineering: field engineers open project folders in the Synology Drive mobile app at a customer site by typing the QuickConnect ID, without a VPN.
Sales: staff in the regional offices and on the road reach the latest price lists and quotation templates in Synology Drive.
Marketing: upload exhibition photos from a phone to Synology Photos during an event.
IT: give remote access to selected NAS services without opening ports on the HQ router.
how_to:
Go to Control Panel > External Access > QuickConnect.
Check that Enable QuickConnect is ticked and note the QuickConnect ID. Sign in with the company's Synology Account if DSM asks for it.
Open the advanced settings and allow only the services staff really need from outside, such as Synology Drive and Synology Photos.
Require 2-step sign-in for all accounts in Control Panel > Security > Account, starting with administrators.
Give staff the QuickConnect ID. In Synology Drive Client or the Synology mobile apps they type it as the server address and sign in with their NAS account.
For browser access from outside, staff go to https://quickconnect.to/ followed by the QuickConnect ID.
tips:
Anyone who knows the QuickConnect ID can reach the sign-in page, so strong passwords and 2-step sign-in are essential.

name: RADIUS Server

HR: when a staff member leaves, disabling their account also stops their Wi-Fi access, with no shared password to change.
IT: replace the shared Wi-Fi password at HQ and regional offices with personal staff sign-ins.

name: Snapshot Replication

use_cases:
Sales: get yesterday's version of a quotation folder back in minutes after someone overwrites or deletes files.

Set a schedule (for example every hour during office hours) and a retention policy.
In the same settings, make snapshots visible so staff can restore files themselves from the #snapshot folder or Windows Previous Versions.
Turn on immutable snapshots for critical folders such as Finance and Sales, with a protection period of, for example, 7 days.
Use the Recovery section to restore a whole folder, and the Replication section to copy snapshots to a second Synology NAS.
Check the Log section regularly for failed snapshots.
tips:
Snapshots live on the same disks as the data; they do not help if the NAS itself fails, so also use Hyper Backup.
Immutable snapshots cannot be deleted early and use space until they expire.
Shared folders must be on a Btrfs volume.

approval_note: Synology publishes it, but it gives full database access, so only IT and SWE use it, and only from the office network.
summary: Web-based tool for managing MariaDB databases: browse tables, run queries, import and export.
description: phpMyAdmin is an open-source web tool from the phpMyAdmin team, published by Synology in Package Center, for managing MariaDB and MySQL databases from a browser. IT and developers can browse and edit tables, run SQL queries, manage database users, and export or import data. It needs Web Station and PHP 8.2, and connects to MariaDB 10.
use_cases:
IT: create a separate database user for each internal application, with only the rights it needs.
SWE: check and fix data in internal tools, such as stock or service-report databases, without command-line tools.
IT: export a database before an upgrade, so it can be restored if something goes wrong.
how_to:
Open Main Menu > phpMyAdmin. It opens in a new browser tab.
Sign in with a MariaDB 10 account (not your DSM account).
Select a database on the left to browse tables, edit records or run SQL.
Use the Export tab to save a backup before making changes. Use Import to restore one.
Under User accounts, create a separate user for each application and give it access only to its own database.
Log out when you finish.
tips:
Never make phpMyAdmin reachable from the internet. Allow it only from the office network or VPN in Control Panel > Security > Firewall.
It needs PHP 8.2. Do not stop or remove PHP 8.2 while phpMyAdmin is installed.
Known limitation: after a fresh install or reinstall, the phpMyAdmin icon is visible only to system administrators.

name: Python2
approval_note: It reached end-of-life in January 2020. If it is installed, move scripts to a supported Python 3 version, then remove it once nothing depends on it.
summary: Python 2 runtime. Support ended in January 2020, so move scripts to Python 3 and remove it.
description: Python is a widely used open-source programming language from the Python Software Foundation; Synology publishes this package in Package Center. It provides Python 2.7.18, the final Python 2 release. Python 2 reached end-of-life in January 2020 and has had no security fixes since then.
use_cases:
IT: find old admin scripts that still run on Python 2 and have them rewritten for Python 3.
SWE: port Python 2 scripts to a supported Python 3 version (3.12 or later).
Management: removing software that has had no support since 2020 lowers the security risk on the NAS.
how_to:
If Python2 is installed, open Package Center > Installed > Python2 and ask IT to confirm whether another installed package depends on it.
Review Control Panel > Task Scheduler and the IT and SWE script folders for anything that calls python2.
Port those scripts to Python 3 and run them on a supported version (3.12 or later), for example in Container Manager.
Run the new and old versions side by side, compare the results, then switch the scheduled tasks to the new versions.
Once nothing uses it, stop and uninstall Python2 from Package Center.
tips:
End-of-life since January 2020. Do not use Python 3.9 as the replacement either, because its support also ended, in October 2025.
Do not uninstall it before checking dependencies. Package Center lists Python2 as a dependency of Download Station, and a scheduled task or script may still need it.
